items.title: Billy McBride and Mary McBride ("Mack and Mack") Interview, 1959-07-01
items.q: Ed Lee had heard so much about us, he wanted to get us to work with him. So we did. And, uh, after he saw that I could produce shows, I was his producer.

ctx.x: And Louis Armstrong, he was out to Miss Joseph's home. That was a home for bad boys. Yes, I remember. And then he would come to the cabaret at night and put on long pants and play with Joe in there, with sneaking plays. Uh-huh.

Well, at first, though, this man, Lou Rosen, we were talking about him, who was a, manager of the Dolphin Theater. He had a company there in Orleans called Lee's Creole Bells, run by Ed Lee. Well, Ed Lee had heard so much about us, he wanted to get us to work with him. So we did. And, uh, after he saw that I could produce shows, I was his producer. And I stayed with him. How long did we stay with Ed Lee up there for Lou Rose? Oh, years. Yes, three or four years. Every summer. You know, we just get tired of being…

We just got tired. You know? They just keep you. Yeah. And the people would go to the show and say, is Mac and Mac here? No. Mac's Mary, no. Well, we're not coming. Then we have to come back. Just keep, just coming back, coming back, coming back. Yeah.
